subject: Integration discovery: BridgeHealth SDK quickstart & on-prem pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@bridgehealth.com>, Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@bridgehealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration discovery recap + suggested quickstart items

Hi Samir / Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get engineering moving on a local proof-of-concept: 

TL;DR: we'll provide a small SDK quickstart for Python + TypeScript, a sample embeddings + reranker demo dataset, and a short on-prem pilot checklist (network + auth requirements). Please confirm the items below so Mateo can scope the deliverables.

What we discussed (high level):
- Primary use case: triage + structured summarization of patient intake forms, then rerank candidate recommendations for clinician review.
- Primary tech stack: Node.js (TS) frontend + Python backend for batch processing.
- Privacy/regulatory: BridgeHealth prefers an on-prem/private deployment for initial pilot and SOC2 evidence.

Proposed quickstart deliverables:
1) SDK quickstart repo (two folders: /python and /typescript) with minimal examples: generate, chat (tool-calling stub), embeddings + local reranker script.
2) Authentication options doc: API key for quick local testing vs OIDC (recommended) for pilot.
3) Routing & model suggestions: latency vs cost-backed recommendations and a fallback policy for high-load bursts.
4) Small sample dataset + instructions for token budgeting and local KV cache usage.

Questions for you (please reply inline):
- Do you want RBWD-hosted (hosted API) for initial POC or strictly private/on-prem?
- Does your infra team require HSM/KMS integration for keys on day 1?
- Any specific firewall/IP restrictions we should list in the on-prem checklist?

Next steps: Mateo will follow up with a technical note + attachments (quickstart zip + network reqs) and I'll propose a 45-min architecture workshop this week.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@bridgehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration discovery recap + suggested quickstart items

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few quick answers inline: 

> Do you want RBWD-hosted (hosted API) for initial POC or strictly private/on-prem?
We'd prefer hosted for the absolute fastest time-to-proof, but need to validate the on-prem path since patient PHI is involved. So: start hosted POC for speed, then pilot on-prem for production.

> Does your infra team require HSM/KMS integration for keys on day 1?
Yes — KMS integration is required for production. For the POC, API keys are fine as long as keys can be rotated and we have an audit trail.

> Any specific firewall/IP restrictions we should list in the on-prem checklist?
We will confirm official rules, but engineering wants the firewall/IP ranges and any egress domain names up front. Also list outbound port ranges and whether mutual TLS is required.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Can you provide a TypeScript sample that demonstrates structured output + a simple tool-calling flow (call an internal lookup and then render result)? Our frontend is TS-heavy and seeing that will help product signoff.
2) Rough cost guidance for embeddings/reranker pilot (approx tokens/month) — ballpark is fine.

I'll loop in our infra lead when we schedule the architecture workshop.

— Elena
Elena Moreno

Subject: Re: Integration discovery recap + suggested quickstart items

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick responses. Per Marissa's plan, I'm attaching a small bundle with: RBWD-quickstart-samples.zip (python + ts quickstarts), a one-page network & firewall checklist (redwood-onprem-network-reqs.pdf), and bridge-mvp-map.xlsx with suggested model/router profiles. High-level notes below: 

Auth & local quickstart
- Quick local testing: API key in env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY). Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... then run python quickstart or npm run dev.
- Production / pilot: we recommend OIDC with your IdP + short-lived service tokens. We support standard OIDC flows and can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping.

Python quickstart (notes)
- venv recommended; pip install redwood==0.6.1 (sample shim)
- sample command: python examples/embeddings_rerank/run_demo.py --data samples/intake_small.json
- run_demo includes TSV output and a minimal reranker that calls the embeddings endpoint, builds FAISS index locally, and scores candidates.

TypeScript quickstart (notes)
- repo/examples/ts has a simple Express endpoint that: accepts a patient summary -> calls /chat with structured-output schema -> demonstrates tool calling by sending a follow-up external lookup request stub (see examples/tools/lookup.ts).
- npm install; copy .env.example -> .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY; npm run dev to start the sample.

Routing & model guidance
- For low-latency UI flows: use the low-latency model profile with prefix caching enabled. For bulk batch rerank, use a cost-optimized quantized model.
- We include an example routing policy in bridge-mvp-map.xlsx that pins N requests/sec to hosted GPUs for the POC and falls back to a smaller variant if capacity spikes.

Network / on-prem checklist (high level)
- Outbound allowed: *.redwoodinference.com (443); IP ranges: 34.120.0.0/16, 35.200.0.0/16 (we'll provide final IP list for the pilot).
- Ports: 443 egress required. mTLS optional but supported.
- KMS/HSM: we support standard KMS API integrations; we will coordinate a short-run on key wrapping and proof-of-concept key exchange.

Attachments included: RBWD-quickstart-samples.zip (src examples), bridge-mvp-map.xlsx (routing + model profiles), redwood-onprem-network-reqs.pdf.

Samir / Elena — if you can confirm a 45 min slot tomorrow or Wednesday for an architecture workshop, I'll prepare a short demo (TS structured output + reranker run).

Thanks,

Mateo Alvarez
